Round 2. A/B/C put a TEXTURE on the lab (glow, notebook, journal) — that is why they felt generic. D and E give it a POSITION instead.

D · FRONTIER — the lab as an instrument. Its thesis drawn as Fig. 1: every gain in AI for code is paid for in compute, energy or opacity, and the lab's job is to move that curve. Archivo Expanded + Martian Mono on technical sage paper. Publications become a data table with citation bars. Confident, peer-facing, zero decoration.

E · THE QUESTIONS — the lab as a list of open questions, answered and not. Straight from Antonio's own paper titles ("Is quantization a deal-breaker?"). Gloock display serif, huge, on white; status chips ANSWERED / IN REVIEW / OPEN. Nobody in SE does this. It recruits, and it is honest about what is unfinished.

Both carry the same real data as the live build. Recruiting lines are bracketed placeholders.
Round 1 (kept for comparison) — A Halo, B Field Notes, C Monograph.
